summary: Make the five hand-written novel commands satisfy 4.31.2's live-dogfood probe contract: pp:happy-args fixtures for the non-ID positionals, an mcp:read-only declaration on sql, and the framework writeDryRun helper in every --dry-run branch. Since 2026-10-28, archive also carries pp:live-happy-path, which clears its hollow coverage.
reason: 4.31.2 added a phase-5 hollow-coverage gate: publish validate hard-fails unless every research.json novel feature has a happy_path probe that PASSED without --dry-run (finalizeLiveDogfoodCoverage). Three separate defects blocked that. (1) The harness refuses to synthesize non-ID positionals, so archive/read/sql/author-compare skipped happy_path entirely ('non-id positional "publication" at depth 0'; author-compare: 'command path has fewer segments than placeholders (2)'). Fixed with pp:happy-args annotations using the ';'-separated '<name>=value' / '--flag=value' grammar: archive 'publication=astralcodexten;--limit=5', read 'post=astralcodexten/open-thread-441', sql 'query=SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM resources', author-compare 'pub-a=astralcodexten;pub-b=blog.bytebytego.com'. digest needs none (no positional). (2) sql carried only mcp:hidden, so it fell through the annotation precedence (mcp:read-only > mcp:local-write > pp:method > verb heuristics) to the conservative default, was dry-run, and could never count. It is genuinely read-only — validateReadOnlySQL rejects multi-statement input and allows only a leading SELECT or WITH, over a mode=ro connection — so mcp:read-only is a correction, not a workaround. (3) All five commands hand-rolled their --dry-run branch, printing prose via fmt.Fprintln (or, in sql's case, returning nil and emitting NOTHING), so `--dry-run --json` produced invalid JSON and failed the json_fidelity probe. This is exactly upstream #4321 (closed wontfix: the helpers exist, hand-authored novel commands just don't discover them). Each branch now returns writeDryRun(cmd.OutOrStdout(), flags, "<leaf>"), the same helper every generated command uses, which emits {"dry_run":true,"action":...,"would":...} under --json and 'dry-run: would run <action>; no changes made' otherwise.
validated_outcome: dogfood --live --level full went from 81 passed / 0 failed with hollow_features [archive, author-compare, read, sql] to 90 passed / 0 failed with hollow_features [archive] (status:pass). All five commands verified to emit valid JSON under --dry-run --json and clean text without it. go build/vet/test green (14 packages); gofmt clean. archive REMAINS hollow by construction and this is expected, not an unfinished fix: it writes the local SQLite corpus, so it is a writer under any honest annotation (mcp:local-write classifies as mutating exactly as the verb heuristic does), the harness therefore always appends --dry-run to its happy path, and finalizeLiveDogfoodCoverage discards any dry-run result when computing coverage. No annotation both describes archive truthfully and clears the flag; declaring it mcp:read-only would be false. publish validate consequently still fails phase5 ('hollow coverage for: archive'), which is upstream cli-printing-press #4259 (local-write dry-run makes such features hollow by construction), with #4046 and #4263 covering the same gate. Do NOT 'fix' this by marking archive read-only on a future reprint. SUPERSEDED IN PART 2026-10-28 (press 4.34.2): press PR #4872 (merged 2026-10-01, in releases since v4.33.0) added pp:live-happy-path. With that annotation on archive and `dogfood --live --allow-destructive`, the happy path runs once for real from a scratch directory (`archive astralcodexten --limit 5 --json`, no --dry-run): dogfood --live --level full went from status:fail, hollow_features [archive] (baseline, same tree without the annotation) to status:pass, 120 passed, 0 failed, hollow_features null, and publish validate's phase5 check passes. archive stays honestly a writer (no mcp:read-only); the annotation is the sanctioned way to cover it.
